tables.name: users
tables.reason: Verify actual source columns, constraints, password-hash compatibility, and profile/auth semantics from a captured schema snapshot.

tables.name: skills
tables.reason: Source ORM defines unique required name String(100), required indexed category String(100), icon default Wrench, nullable description String(255), and popularity default 0. Target Skill requires a unique normalizedName, limits name/category to 80 characters, defaults category to Other, permits description up to 500 characters, omits icon/popularity, and adds createdBy. Define normalization, collision handling, truncation/rejection policy, and treatment of icon/popularity before approval; verify live constraints and values from a captured PostgreSQL snapshot.

tables.name: user_skills
tables.reason: Source ORM defines user_id and skill_id as required indexed foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE, skill_type String(20) required (source comment: OFFERED or NEEDED), experience_level default Intermediate, nullable description Text, and created_at. Target stores skill ObjectId arrays directly on User and has no per-association experience_level, description, or created_at. Verify actual type values and constraints, map OFFERED/NEEDED deliberately to teach/learn, resolve numeric source IDs to target ObjectIds, and decide how association metadata is preserved before approval.

tables.name: exchanges
tables.reason: Source ORM defines required requester_id and receiver_id user FKs (ON DELETE CASCADE); nullable requester_skill_id and receiver_skill_id skill FKs (ON DELETE SET NULL); status String(30), default PENDING, with source comment listing PENDING/COUNTERED/REJECTED/ACTIVE/COMPLETED/CANCELLED; required proposal_message; nullable counter_message, preferred_date String(100), location_area String(200), cancellation_reason String(255), and cancelled_by_id (users FK ON DELETE SET NULL); estimated_hours default 2.0; requester_completed and receiver_completed default false; created_at and updated_at. Target requires both skillOffered and skillRequested, uses message and scheduledAt instead of proposal/counter/preferred-date/location fields, and restricts status to a different lowercase enum. Decide how to represent missing skills, map every observed status explicitly, preserve scheduling/cancellation data and mutual completion flags, and verify actual constraints/status values from the captured PostgreSQL schema before approval.

tables.name: messages
tables.reason: Source ORM defines required indexed sender_id and receiver_id user foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE; nullable indexed exchange_id foreign key with ON DELETE SET NULL; required content Text; is_read Boolean default false; and created_at timestamp defaulting to UTC now and indexed. Target Message instead requires exchange, sender, recipient, and body; body is trimmed and capped at 5000 characters, read state is represented by nullable readAt, and timestamps are automatic createdAt/updatedAt. Define how nullable exchange references are preserved despite the required target exchange, map content to body with an explicit overlength policy, convert numeric source IDs to ObjectIds, and handle is_read=true when the source has no read timestamp. Verify actual source constraints, indexes, and values from a captured PostgreSQL snapshot before approval.

tables.name: reviews
tables.reason: Source ORM defines required indexed exchange_id, reviewer_id, and reviewee_id foreign keys with ON DELETE CASCADE; required integer rating with a source comment indicating 1–5 stars; reliability_score and skill_quality_score default 5; would_exchange_again Boolean default true; nullable comment Text; created_at timestamp; and unique constraint uq_exchange_reviewer on (exchange_id, reviewer_id). Target Review enforces rating min 1/max 5 and a unique (exchange, reviewer) index, but has no reliability_score, skill_quality_score, or would_exchange_again fields, trims comment and caps it at 2000 characters, and uses automatic createdAt/updatedAt. Verify actual source rating/sub-score constraints and observed values, decide how to preserve or intentionally transform sub-scores and would_exchange_again, define a policy for comments longer than 2000 characters, convert numeric IDs to ObjectIds, and confirm target uniqueness matches source semantics before approval.

tables.name: posts
tables.reason: Verify content, author, tags, likes, visibility, and relationship fields.

tables.name: notifications
tables.reason: Source ORM model defines user_id (required, users FK ON DELETE CASCADE), type String(50) required, title String(150) required, message Text required, nullable link String(255), is_read Boolean default false, and created_at. Target Notification instead requires a recipient and restricts type to a fixed lowercase enum, stores body instead of message, derives read state from readAt, adds actor/resource fields, and uses automatic timestamps. Keep mapping pending until actual source type values, source constraints, and an explicit conversion for type/message/link/read state are reviewed.

tables.name: blocks
tables.reason: Source ORM model defines id, blocker_id, blocked_id, and created_at; blocker_id and blocked_id reference users.id with ON DELETE CASCADE, both are indexed, and uq_blocker_blocked enforces pair uniqueness. Target Block model mirrors the relationship shape, but keep mapping pending until the captured PostgreSQL constraints, indexes, nullability/defaults, row counts, and any RLS policies are verified against the live source snapshot.

tables.name: reports
tables.reason: Source ORM model defines reporter_id (required, users FK ON DELETE CASCADE), reported_user_id (nullable, users FK ON DELETE CASCADE), reported_exchange_id (nullable, exchanges FK ON DELETE SET NULL), required category String(50), required details Text, status default PENDING (source comment lists PENDING/RESOLVED/DISMISSED), nullable admin_note Text, and created_at. Target Report currently uses targetType/targetId, reason, details, lowercase statuses, resolutionNote/resolvedBy, and automatic createdAt/updatedAt; this is not a field-for-field match. Keep mapping pending until source constraints and actual status values are reviewed and a deliberate transformation is specified, including user-only and exchange-only reports.

tables.name: analytics_events
tables.reason: Approve retention/privacy rules and verify event/property schema before deciding which data may migrate.

tables.name: connections
tables.reason: Source columns, foreign keys, uniqueness, indexes, and source application code support a dedicated user-to-user community Connection model, separate from exchanges. Target model is provisional only; inventory status values and source row semantics, then review the complete schema snapshot before approving field mappings or import.
